newsitem.title: USA: U.S. condemns violence on Belgrade protesters.
newsitem.headline: U.S. condemns violence on Belgrade protesters.

text.p: The United States on Monday condemned what it called "the most serious use of force" against demonstrators in Belgrade over the weekend and urged Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to exercise restraint.

"The United States strongly condemns the violence by the Serbian police against the demonstrators who by all accounts have demonstrated peacefully. We call on the Serb police and the Serb authorities led by President Milosevic to exercise restraint in the streets of Belgrade," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
Burns told a briefing the government action "will only further Serbia's isolation (and) deepen the political crisis in Belgrade. This is an extremely discouraging set of events."
He said that after Sunday's use by Serb police of batons and water cannons on protesters demanding democratic changes in Belgrade, he understood there had been further police violence on Monday.

The U.S. charge d'affaires in Belgrade met Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic on Monday morning "to condemn the police action and to call upon the Serbian government officially to refrain from using police force in the streets of Belgrade..."
Burns said the diplomat had also met an opposition leader, Vuk Draskovic, to "express our support for the opposition's track record of peaceful protest and to counsel restraint on all sides."
